audits.text:
## b650a355848c

**Reproduced generator-domain defect: nearest-marker assignments are frequently
ambiguous or non-bijective.** Across 8,000 ordinary draws (bands default/easy/
medium/hard; seeds 0–99; sample indices 0–19), 2,104 had at least one equal-distance
nearest-marker tie and 4,162 mapped two or more shapes to the same marker. All
4,162 consequently left at least one distinct marker unused even though the
generator summary and invariant present equal counts as paired teaching signals.

The retained seed `0`, sample index `1`, default band passes `self_check` but its
three shape-to-marker distance rows are `[3,4,2]`, `[6,4,4]`, and `[11,11,4]`.
The selected Racket rule's reverse-row-major tie order assigns color `3` to all
three output shapes. A plausible one-to-one minimum-total-distance interpretation
instead uses all marker colors `9,1,3`; the outputs differ. This is in the
documented ordinary generator domain, not merely the validator envelope.

Evidence: `checks/audit/b650a355848c/finding.json`, `input.json`, `racket.json`,
and `rival.json`. The supported authority command and exact generator/rule hashes
are recorded in `racket.json`; the bounded census is in
`checks/audit/b650_probe.json`. Suggested repair: place markers only after checking
that each shape has one strictly nearest marker and that the nearest mapping is a
bijection, or explicitly redesign the task contract to teach tie and reuse behavior.
